Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-20. The blindness rule bit hard today: news-log entries dated 23 November (futures up 2-3% after the seven-day rout, CrowdStrike's $43.9B offer for Zscaler, gold rebounding 3% off its lows, crude sliding on Russia-Ukraine peace-deal progress) were NOT used, and neither were Saxo Bank's 23 November capitulation-gauge brief, Tickmill's 23 November GS Panic Index reading, the Motley Fool's 21 November Thanksgiving-week seasonality piece, Wolf Street's 21 November Treasury wrap, the Vito Report's 22 November weekly review or FXEmpire's 23 November week-ahead calendar with its consensus figures. The 23-27 November data calendar is cited only from sources dated 20 November itself (Kitco's wrap and stockmarketwatch's Market Digest), and no earnings calendar for that week dated at or before 20 November was obtained.

Two sigma inputs were upgraded from long-stale carries to real dated numbers this session, and one was not. The Russell 2000's sigma moves from the 19.97 RVX value this ledger had carried since 23 September to the actual RVX close of 36.88 on 20 November (Cboe RVX dashboard, cross-checked exactly against FRED's RVXCLS 30.46 on 19 November plus the dashboard's +6.42 change). That materially changes the overlay for that asset: on the stale 19.97 its stretch score was -3 (extreme-down), which would have vetoed or notched any bearish small-cap call; on the real 36.88 it is -1 (neutral) and the overlay takes no action. The wider, honest sigma also widens the Russell's bands from 0.63%/1.41%/1.99% to 1.16%/2.60%/3.67%. The dollar's sigma moves from 4.72 (carried from 21 September) to EUR/USD one-month at-the-money implied volatility of 6.10% as of the 13 November close (Cross Vol Research, 14 November), which takes its z50 from 6.45 to 4.99 and its z200 from 12.88 to 9.97 but leaves the stretch score at +4. Bonds' sigma is still the TLT 30-day implied-volatility value of 15 carried from 25 September, now 38 sessions stale: the ICE BofA MOVE index at 96.04 on 19 November (StreetStats) is the only dated Treasury-volatility number obtained and it cannot be converted into a ZN=F percentage sigma without inventing a conversion. With VIX at 35.89 the carried 15 very likely understates bond volatility and so narrows that asset's bands.

News-log entries for 2026-11-20 (four, matching the Artifact database exactly - the query returned the same four ids already present in data/news_log.json, so no merge was needed, and there were no hand-entered 'manual (issue #N)' entries for this date) were read and used. The session wrap is CappNotes' 'Closing Look - Friday, November 20, 2026', which supplied indexes, breadth, all 11 sectors, VIX, the full Treasury curve, credit spreads, FX crosses, metals, oil, crypto, ETF flows, Kalshi and Barchart pricing, the UMich release and movers. stockmarketwatch's 'Market Digest - Friday, November 20, 2026' supplied sector-ETF detail (SMH -10.60%, BAI -9.67%) and the 23-25 November data calendar; Kitco's 20 November gold and silver wrap supplied the metals ranking language, the named analyst commentary and the same data calendar; AP and UPI closing data supplied the weekly index returns and the correction framing; Reuters (via Yahoo Finance and 24/7 Wall St., 20 November) supplied the Nvidia SEC accounting-inquiry report; AAII's survey for the week ending 18 November supplied sentiment; Cboe and FRED supplied RVX. Categories 1-12 are neutral unless a dated source gives a clear read, and today a lot of them are genuinely two-sided. Sentiment is a contrarian bullish vote at 5 and 10 sessions for the equity assets on AAII's 42.2% bearish (41st straight week above the 31.5% average, surveyed through 18 November, i.e. before Friday's decline) and for gold on the four named analysts calling its selling excessive. Positioning is bullish at 5 and 10 sessions for the equity assets on the CTA and de-grossing readings and for gold at 5 sessions on TD Securities' possible CTA short-covering. Earnings catalysts is bearish for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 on Nvidia's 14.01% fall to a 52-week low on the SEC accounting report, Intuit -12.77% and beats being sold, but neutral for the Russell 2000, where Gap +11.44% and Buckle +5.67% genuinely offset BJ's -5.35% and Ross -2.92%. Macro calendar is bullish at 1 session for the equity assets on UMich sentiment 51.5 with one-year inflation expectations falling to 3.7% from 4.3%, bearish at 5 sessions for everything but the dollar on 25 November's PCE against hot dated priors (October PPI +6.5% y/y, Philadelphia Fed prices paid 58.2 from 43.2), and bullish at 5 sessions for the dollar on the same facts. Seasonality is neutral at every cell: the long-run Thanksgiving-week statistics obtainable here average roughly +0.3%, which sits inside every asset's 1-session band, and the pieces carrying them could not be dated at or before 20 November. Cross-asset (1D and 5D) is bearish for all three equity assets and gold on the liquidation tape, bullish for Treasuries, and neutral then bullish for the dollar; 10 sessions is neutral everywhere because the same facts - forced selling across assets with four of six assets deeply oversold at once - genuinely cut both ways. Trend structure follows the computed structure reads and says so where they are choppy or where a computed uptrend has already broken its last higher low; Market structure carries its own mechanical direction.
